1,3-Stereocontrol in Stereoconvergent Allenylic Alkylation Enabled
by Palladium and Chiral Phase-Transfer Cooperative Catalysis
Hongbo Qi,* Wenhua Wu, and Dan-Xing Wu

ABSTRACT: A stereoconvergent allenylic alkylation of allenyl acetates with oxindoles has been established by palladium and chiral
phase-transfer cooperative catalysis, allowing for an efficient construction of 1,3-nonadjacent stereogenic elements featuring both
central and axial chirality. The noncovalent interactions of PTC create a chiral environment for nucleophilic attack on η
3
-
allylpalladium intermediates. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Pd/PTC synergistic action and matched chirality are both
critical for stereocontrol, while PTC primarily determines the stereoselectivity. Notably, this work represents the first successful
implementation of Pd/chiral PTC dual catalysis for 1,3-nonadjacent stereocontrol, thereby enriching the synthetic toolbox for
constructing challenging remote stereocenters.
A
symmetric catalysis stands at the forefront of modern
organic synthesis, enabling the stereocontrolled assembly
of enantioenriched molecules vital to pharmaceuticals, agro-
chemicals, and functional materials.
1
The prevalence of
multiple stereogenic elements in bioactive molecules
2
has
made stereoselective construction a long-standing research
focus in organic synthesis.
3
Despite remarkable advances in
vicinal stereocenter construction, the precise control of
nonadjacent stereocenters remains a persistent challenge.
4
Three interrelated factors contribute to this synthetic
challenge:
5
(i) the flexible transition state emerges as a critical
barrier to reliable remote stereocontrol; (ii) asymmetric
induction efficiency declines with greater stereocenter
separation; and (iii) nonadjacent stereocenter formation
produces ≥4 stereoisomers, increasing synthetic complexity.
Chiral allenes represent a privileged class of structural motifs
found in natural products, bioactive molecules and functional
materials.
6
Consequently, the design of efficient synthetic
routes to chiral allenes has become a major objective in organic
synthesis, and significant advances have recently been achieved
in the field of constructing single allenyl axial chirality.
7
Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric allenylic alkylation
represents a powerful strategy for the stereoselective
construction of enantioenriched allene derivatives with precise
stereocontrol.
7d,8,9
Notably, allenyl axial chirality with vicinal
central chirality could be controllably installed using transition-
metal-catalyzed.
8g,10
However, the simultaneous control of
remote stereocenters featuring both allenyl axial chirality and
central chirality remains limited,
8i,j,9
despite the fact that such
scaffolds play a significant role in medicinal chemistry and
synthetic chemistry.
11
In 2023, two distinct Pd/chiral amine
dual catalyst systems were independently developed by Mi and
Luo
9e
and Li and Shao
9b
for allylic allenylation reactions of β-
ketocarbonyl and aldehyde, respectively, enabling the 1,3-
nonadjacent stereocenters with allenyl axial chirality and
central chirality to be stereoselectively controlled. Subse-
quently, Wen and Guo described a Pd/chiral aldehyde
cooperatively catalyzed asymmetric allenylic alkylation of
unprotected amino acid esters, providing an efficient access
to these valuable scaffolds (Scheme 1a).
9f
Beyond metal/
organocatalytic approaches, bimetallic catalysis has proven
highly effective for precise stereocontrol in constructing these
scaffolds, as demonstrated by Zhang and Ma
8j,9g
and He
9h
and
Lin.
9a
Chiral PTCs are important type of organocatalysts and have
grown to be indispensable tools for asymmetric synthesis,

12
Notably, this system faces
heightened background reactivity relative to classical organo-
catalysts. Additionally, PTC systems feature a single activation
site, specifically a chiral cationic center that mediates ionic
interactions, restricting the simultaneous activation of both
reaction partners. This limitation prompted developing PTC-
based dual catalytic systems with secondary activation modes,
significantly broadening synthetic applications.
13
Since the Pd/
chiral PTC-catalyzed asymmetric allylic alkylation of Schiff
bases reported by Gong
14a
and Takemoto,
14b
transition metal/
chiral PTC combined catalysis has emerged as a highly
promising strategy in asymmetric catalysis.
15
However, such
catalytic systems have rarely been applied to simultaneously
and stereoselectively construct 1,3-nonadjacent stereocenters
(Scheme 1b). We herein report a Pd/chiral PTC-catalyzed
enantioselective allenylic alkylation, simultaneously creating
allenyl axial chirality and all-carbon quaternary stereocenters
with excellent enantioselectivity and diastereoselectivity
(Scheme 1c).
We initiated a systematic study of the Pd/chiral PTC-
catalyzed asymmetric allenylic alkylation using racemic
allenylic acetate 1a and oxindole 2a as model substrates
(Table 1). Several commercially available ligands (L1−L4)
were evaluated in the presence of an L -isoleucine-derived
quaternary phosphonium salt (PTC-1). While these systems
could deliver the desired allylic allenylation product 3aa, both
the enantioselectivity and diastereoselectivity proved unsat-
isfactory (entries 1−4). The observed suboptimal stereo-
control may be attributed to competing background reactivity
mediated by a single Pd/ligand catalytic cycle. Inspired by
findings from Takemoto
14b
and Zi,
15f
the deliberate use of
electronically more defficeint phosphite ligand L5 would be
able to slow down the competing monocatalytic process.
Remarkably, this approach not only substantially enhanced
enantioselectivity but also significantly improved diastereose-
lectivity, albeit at the expense of the reaction yield (entry 5).
Subsequently, screening of various phase-transfer catalysts
(PTCs) identified PTC-3 as the optimal, demonstrating
remarkable enhancement in the yield, diastereoselectivity,
and enantioselectivity. These results strongly suggest a
synergistic catalytic effect between ligands L5 and PTC-3, as
evidenced by comparative evaluation of different PTC systems
(entry 7). Base optimization (entries 11−15) identified NaOH

Systematic optimization of other reaction parameters, includ-
ing catalyst loading, base stoichiometry, and reaction time,
found that increased yields and slightly improved stereo-
selectivity were obtained upon using slightly increased
amounts of the palladium catalyst and chiral PTC (entries
16 and 17).
With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we next
explored the substrate generality of the Pd/chiral PTC-
catalyzed asymmetric allenyl alkylation reaction. We first
examined the scope of allenyl acetates 1 (Scheme 2). The
presence of a fluoro, chloro, and methyl group on the benzene
ring at the para- position could smoothly provide the products
3ab−3ad in good yields and excellent stereoselectivities (dr
>91:9, >94% ee). However, a highly electron-donating
substituent is detrimental to the reaction rate and stereo-
selectivity as exemplified by the 4-OMe-substituted substrate,
which delivered the product 3ae in moderate yield and eroded
diastereoselectivity (dr 88:12). Gratifyingly, the good isolated
yield and stereoselectivities were secured for target product 3af
when a substrate possessing an electron-withdrawing group
(−CN) at the para- position of the benzene ring was
employed. The substitution pattern of the aromatic ring
significantly influenced the outcomes. As a result, the
substituent (−Cl, −Me) at either the meta or ortho position
underwent reaction smoothly, yielding products 3ag−3ai with
good stereoselectivity (dr >91:9, >92% ee). A 2-naphthyl-
substituted allenic acetate (2j) proved compatible, furnishing
3aj in 63% yield with 90:10 dr and 94% ee. The protocol also
accommodated the heteroaryl allenic substrates. For example,
the thiophene-functionalized substrate participated in the
reaction to afford 3ak in 70% yield with excellent stereo-
selectivity (dr 94:6, 95% ee). For alkyl substituted substrates,
linear alkyl allenic acetates were reactive substrates, leading to
3al and 3am in acceptable yields (59−65%) and high
enantioselectivities (ee >90%), but diastereoselectivity was
rather poor. Trisubstituted allenyl acetate 2n could participate
in the reaction with excellent enantioselectivity (>92% ee), but
gave moderate yield. The absolute configuration of 3aa was
unambiguously determined by single-crystal X-ray analysis.
Notably, the reaction scalability was confirmed through a 1.0
mmol scale preparation of 3aa.
We next evaluated the reaction scope with respect to
oxindoles 2 (Scheme 3). The catalytic system demonstrated a
broad tolerance for diverse electronic perturbations at the
para-position of the C3-aryl group. Both electron-withdrawing
(−F, −Cl) and electron-donating (−Me, −OMe) substituents
participated in the reaction, smoothly, affording the products
3ba−3ea in good yields and stereoselectivities (dr >90:10,
>91% ee). The method proved equally effective for meta-
substituted C3-aryl oxindoles. Either chloro or methyl
substituted substrate delivered the products 3fa and 3ga in
good yields and excellent stereoselectivity (dr >91:9, ee
>93%). Expansion to larger aromatic systems was also
successful, as shown in the case with the 2-naphthyl substrate,
which furnished 3ha in 65% yield with 90:10 dr and 95% ee.
However, the system showed clear limitations with alkyl
substituents at C3. Neither methyl nor benzyl substituted
oxindoles generated target products 3ia and 3ja, likely due to
the diminished acidity of the C3−H bond in alkyl-substituted
substrates. The protocol exhibited excellent compatibility with
C5-substituted oxindoles. Halogenated substrates (3ka and
3la) underwent the reaction with excellent stereocontrol (dr
>90:10, >95% ee), while electron-rich variants (3ma and 3na)

substituted oxindoles bearing a fluoro (3oa), chloro (3pa), or
methoxy (3qa) group performed admirably, providing
products with good enantioselectivity (>94% ee).
To elucidate the reaction pathway, a series of mechanistic
investigations were conducted (Scheme 4). First, some related
control experiments were performed (Scheme 4a). No product
formation occurred in the absence of the chiral ligand (Scheme
4a, entry 2), confirming its essential role in this transformation.
Omitting chiral PTC yielded almost racemic 3aa (ee <10%)
with poor diastereocontrol (Scheme 4a, entry 3). The result
underscores the dual role of chiral PTC in both phase-transfer
activation and enantioselective nucleophile delivery. Config-
uration inversion of either L5 or PTC-3 significantly eroded
diastereoselectivity (Scheme 4a, entries 4 and 5), demonstrat-
ing that chiral complementarity between the phosphine ligand
and phase-transfer catalyst is essential for optimal stereocontrol
in this dual catalytic system. This matched/mismatched
phenomenon suggests cooperative transition-state organization
involving both chiral elements. Notably, ent-PTC-3 generated
products with inverted enantiomeric excess (ee) values. These
observations collectively demonstrate that the phase tranfer
catalyst serves as the primary determinant of the stereo-
selectivity in this transformation. To probe potential kinetic
resolution effects, the reaction was performed by using
enantiomerically pure (R)- and (S)-1a as substrates (Scheme
4b). Intriguingly, both enantiomers efficiently underwent the
asymmetric alkylation, affording the products with the same
configuration, in similar yields and with identical enantiose-
lectivity. This observation suggests that the quick racemization
allows both substrate enantiomers of 1a to be funneled into a
single product stereoisomer, leading to the enantioconvergent
nature.
The proposed mechanism involves two catalytic cycles, as
illustrated in Scheme 5. In the PTC cycle, PTC+ transfers the
base OH- from the solid base to the organic phase. The enol
form of 2a undergoes deprotonation by the base, generating a
tightly associated nucleophilic ion pair (I) with PTC
+
, along
with one equivalent of water. In the pal-ladium catalysis cycle,
oxidative addition of Pd(0) to ra-cemic allene 1a to form both
η
3
-allylpalladium interme-diate (R)-II and (S)-II, which rapidly
equilibrates via η
1
-allylpalladium intermediate III. The (S)-II
intermediate is kinetically favored over its (R)-II counterpart
for nucleo-philic attack by the chiral ion pair I. This
preferential re-activity pathway enables the highly stereo-
selective in-termolecular asymmetric remote alkenylation,
ultimately leading to the formation of product 3aa with
excellent stereocontrol. In summary, we have established a
stereoconvergent enantioselective allenylic alkylation of
oxindoles with allenyl acetates enabled by cooperative catalysis
of the chiral palladium complex and phase-transfer catalyst
(PTC), leading to the highly stereoselective construction of
1,3-nonadjacent stereogenic elements featuring both central
and axial chirality. The key to successful stereocontrol is the
use of PTC’s noncovalent interactions to establish a chiral
environment for the stereoselective nucleophilic addition to
the η
3
-allylpalladium intermediates. Mechanistic studies reveal
that the synergistic cooperation between the palladium catalyst
and PTC, along with their matched chirality, plays a critical
role in enabling excellent reaction performance (Scheme 5).
This work significantly expands the scope of PTC applications
in metal/organo cocatalysis. We anticipate that this strategy
will provide a general platform for the stereoselective
construction of remotely functionalized chiral centers in
more challenging contexts.
